title: NHS England issues new guidance on children's eating disorder services
source: Healthcare Management UK (reporting NHS England guidance)
summary: NHS England has published new national guidance for children's eating disorder services, reported as developed with Beat and the Royal College of Psychiatrists. It tells professionals not to rely on body size or weight-based thresholds alone when deciding who needs treatment, and to give more weight to behaviour changes and family concerns. Online training is also being offered to teachers, GPs and school nurses to help spot signs earlier.
forParents: If you are worried about your child, your concerns should count in an assessment, and weight alone should not decide whether they get help. If you feel you are being turned away, you can point to this guidance and ask for a specialist assessment. This summary is based on news coverage, so check the NHS England guidance itself for exact wording.

title: Compulsive exercise group added to inpatient care: no extra benefit found
summary: A randomised trial of 75 teenagers aged 12-17 with anorexia in hospital tested a 7-session group aimed at compulsive exercise on top of usual treatment. Both the group that received it and the group that did not improved on compulsive exercise and eating disorder symptoms, with no clear difference between them. About a third of participants did not complete the study, and outcomes were self-reported.
forParents: Intensive, team-based treatment appeared to help with exercise-related urges on its own, though this was a small study and it does not show what happens at home. If compulsive exercise is a worry for your child, raise it with their treatment team.
